name: Feature Engineering Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for feature engineering work: a short set of checks to run before calling a feature engineering task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for feature engineering work: a short set of checks to run before calling a feature engineering task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting feature engineering work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Keep feature engineering outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. Check that feature engineering terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to feature engineering (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Keep feature engineering changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. When multiple feature engineering strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Validate feature engineering outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. Prefer explicit, readable feature engineering solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. When feature engineering guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Measure before optimizing any feature engineering bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting feature engineering assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated feature engineering concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of feature engineering correctness.
- Avoid introducing new feature engineering abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic feature engineering advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about feature engineering over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
